data.title: Pos Malaysia transitions to EVs for a third of its parcel deliveries
data.description: Malaysia's national postal and parcel service provider, Pos Malaysia, has announced it now delivers one in three parcels using EVs. The company has deployed electric vehicles for delivery operations across the country, including Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

data.title: “L” is for “Luxury”: first seat test in the Xpeng G9L
data.description: For almost four years now, Xpeng has produced the G9. Last year, it received its first facelift, and this year, it gained a big brother: the G9L. This model is already available on the Chinese domestic market and is soon set to land in Europe. Xpeng will unveil the massive SUV at the Paris Motor Show and will only then release all the details. In the meantime, we were given an early opportunity to take a seat in the G9L - here's our first impressions.

data.title: VW ID. Tiguan premiere: ID.4 successor starts at €42,695
data.description: In early 2027, Volkswagen will replace its E-SUV ID.4 and its derivative ID.5 with the ID. Tiguan - emphasising its kinship with the best-selling combustion-engine Tiguan. The new VW ID. Tiguan offers drivetrains with up to 220 kW, range of up to 600 km, and towing capacities of up to two tonnes.

data.title: Audi A2 e-tron launches in UK from £32,200
data.description: Audi has opened UK order books for the new A2 e-tron, with prices starting at £32,200 OTR. Deliveries of the compact electric car are expected to reach UK customers from early 2027.

data.title: India: Kolkata Police to induct 183 electric motorcycles
data.description: The police department of Kolkata, the capital of the eastern Indian state West Bengal, has announced plans to add 183 electric motorcycles to its fleet. It has taken delivery of the first 60 units, and once it procures the remaining 123 units, the rollout will represent one of the largest electric motorcycle deployments by any police force in the country.

data.title: VW recalls another 22,524 ID.4 vehicles due to fire risk
data.description: Volkswagen has announced another recall in the US for 22,524 ID.4 units. Until a final solution is available, affected vehicles should only be charged up to a maximum of 80 per cent.

data.title: Cell bypass aims to extend the usable life of EV batteries
data.description: A study by Chalmers University of Technology examines reconfigurable battery packs that can selectively bypass weaker cells. Under optimal conditions, this could extend the lifespan of batteries in certain high-voltage vehicles by more than 20 per cent.

data.title: E.ON Drive takes over BP Pulse fast-charging network in the Netherlands
data.description: E.ON Drive Infrastructure is taking over the former BP Pulse fast-charging network in the Netherlands and will operate it under the Essent brand in the future. The network comprises a total of 79 locations with 370 charging points.

data.title: California: $28m in funding for public EV fast chargers
data.description: The State of California has opened a new $28 million funding round for its existing Fast Charge California Project. This will see it offer up to $100,000 per charging port for DC fast chargers, with applications due to close on 14 January 2027.

data.title: Voltix opens France’s most powerful truck charging station
data.description: In Vierzon, Voltix has opened its first public fast-charging station for electric HGVs. The facility initially offers four charging points, each with up to 1.5 MW - with this later set to expand to eight charging points.

data.title: Fraunhofer opens research centre in Braunschweig
data.description: The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft has inaugurated the new Center for Energy Storage and Systems (ZESS) in Braunschweig. The federal government and the state have invested nearly €50 million euros in the research hub, which focuses on solid-state batteries, cell production, and hydrogen technologies, among other areas.

data.title: EU apparently considering import restrictions for Chinese hybrids
data.description: After China rejected voluntary export restrictions on hybrid cars to the EU, the European Commission is now preparing import restrictions for such vehicles via a safeguard procedure. However, this could also just be a pressure tactic to negotiate a deal, as both parties have entered talks in Beijing regarding the matter.

data.title: One in six new Mercedes passenger cars worldwide now fully electric
data.description: Mercedes-Benz Group sold 78,100 electric vehicles in the third quarter. These accounted for 16 per cent of all Mercedes cars and vans sold worldwide - up by more than six percentage points compared to the same period last year. However, China remains an extremely challenging market for the Stuttgart-based company.

data.title: Schools could lead India’s private bus transition, World Bank expert says
data.description: India's transition to zero-emission buses has so far been driven largely by public transport authorities (PTAs). However, public fleets represent only 8 to 10 per cent of the country's bus market, while private operators account for around 90 per cent or approximately 1.6 million buses. A broader transition in the bus segment will thus happen only when the private sector accelerates adoption.

data.title: Traton R&D chief: ‘Are we considering LFP? Yes, absolutely’
data.description: The Traton Group is investing heavily in new drive technologies. Niklas Klingenberg, the group’s top development executive, is one of the key decisionmakers shaping the truck technology of tomorrow at MAN and Scania. We spoke to Klingenberg about group dynamics, battery chemistries and China’s role in the technology race.

data.title: DeepDrive secures high-volume order for electric drive systems starting in 2028
data.description: According to its own statements, DeepDrive has been nominated as a mass-production supplier for an unnamed global vehicle manufacturer. The start of series production for the Munich-based company's electric drive is planned for 2028. In parallel, DeepDrive is establishing a presence in China.

data.title: BMW iX4 arrives as an electric SUV-coupé starting at €70,900
data.description: BMW continues to expand its 'Neue Klasse' family with the new iX4, a sporty electric SUV coupé positioned between the iX3 and larger iX5. The model will launch in three all-wheel-drive variants, including the 450 kW iX4 M60 xDrive. Prices start at €70,900.

data.title: 100 km/h in 3.9 seconds: BMW unveils upgraded iX3
data.description: BMW is presenting the most powerful drivetrain variant of its premium iX3 eSUV to date. The new BMW iX3 M60 xDrive takes the lead in the lineup with 450 kW and is said to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in under four seconds. The Munich-based manufacturer plans to open order books at the end of January 2027.

data.title: Researchers explore potential of lithium-sulphur batteries
data.description: Researchers from Vanderbilt University and the University of Maryland have presented a new cell chemistry that could significantly increase the energy density of lithium-sulphur batteries. By integrating chlorine, the approach enables additional electron transfer at higher voltage.

data.title: Driving the Leapmotor B03X reveals a spacious electric car that lacks polish
data.description: Leapmotor is growing in Europe with Stellantis backing. Now, the Chinese brand aims to make its mark in the small electric SUV segment with the B03X, focusing on space and clever ideas. A first test drive reveals whether the crossover delivers on its promises.
